## Before M1: review y-sweet

[y-sweet](/discussion/prior-art/#y-sweet) is an open-source Rust server for Yjs documents, built on Yrs, with persistence and per-document access tokens. It may already be most of what hosting needs. Before any hosting code is written, review it for reuse:

- **Fit:** can it host Xmesh documents, and carry XTXP's own messages (identity, binding, grants) alongside Yjs sync?
- **Access control:** how its client tokens compare with XTXP's [key-based grants](/spec/identity/), and whether ours can replace or wrap them.
- **Branching:** whether forking a document at a state vector and merging back fits its storage model.
- **Storage:** its persistence (filesystem, S3-compatible) against XTXP's append-then-compact plan.
- **Hosting:** it can run as a binary or as Wasm on Cloudflare's edge, which bears on the [hosting question](/discussion/open-questions/#engine).
- **Health:** licence, maintenance activity, and how easily it can be extended without forking.

The outcome decides whether hosting extends y-sweet, borrows from it, or starts fresh.

## M1 — Headless convergence

Three CLI peers (Rust, embedding Xmesh), one of them a late joiner that loads the full state, connect over WebSocket to a headless MUPPET hosting the branch and replay the fuzzer's vectors, with connections dropped on purpose to exercise reconnect sync. Each peer authenticates by key and binds its client ID. There is no UI. This proves convergence over a patchy network and the identity handshake before anyone draws anything.

## M2 — Inkscape plus no-JS

The Inkscape fork, linking Xmesh through its C interface, and a plain HTML browser served by a server-side MUPPET edit the same drawing. This is the first demo a person can see, and it tests the north star directly.

## M3 — Inkscape plus Wasm

A Wasm MUPPET in the browser joins as a full peer.

## M4 — Inkscape plus Conversations

Mobile and chat users take part through the XMPP bridge. What a stock Conversations user gets is [open question 7](/discussion/open-questions/#q7-what-does-a-conversations-user-get-in-m4).

## Where the gateway fits

The xtxp.link gateway and live web branching don't have a milestone yet. See [open question 9](/discussion/open-questions/#q9-where-does-the-web-gateway-sit-in-the-milestones). Folding it into M2 is a strong candidate, since the no-JS path of M2 *is* the gateway.

## Roadmap

Deferred until the first milestones show they're needed. Each one starts by checking what the Yrs toolchain already offers.

| Item | Why deferred | Until then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Ledger**: a chronological patch log in cold storage, for unbounded, branchable undo | The Yjs ecosystem already persists documents by appending updates and compacting them | Append-and-compact storage per branch |
| **Keyframes**: hot snapshots tuned for instant loading | Yrs can encode a whole document as one compact update | The full state as one update |
| **History limits and garbage collection** | Snapshots need Yrs's garbage collection off, so deleted content is kept | Keep everything; measure growth |
| **Native C++ Xmesh** | Yrs is already native code; a rewrite would be about owning the engine, not speed | Xmesh on Yrs, through its C interface |
| **Elixir / BEAM hosting** | Worth considering at large scale, for the BEAM's supervision and clustering | Rust hosting, one actor per branch |
| **Signed hash chains** of each client's operations | Signing only at identity steps is enough to start | Authorship from client bindings |
